issues.observed: The four KPI values are large but have no visible titles, so executives cannot reliably distinguish Total Revenue, Gross Margin, YoY Growth, and Risk Areas.
issues.desired: Each KPI card should have a persistent business label, correctly formatted value, and concise comparison or status context.
issues.action: Enable category labels or add fixed titles above every card. Use labels such as Total Revenue, Gross Margin, YoY Growth, and Risk Areas; retain the existing measure semantics and validate that percentage and currency formats come from the model.

issues.observed: MonthName is displayed in a non-chronological sequence, including April, August, December, February, January, and July. The connected lines therefore imply trends that did not occur in that order.
issues.desired: Time-series charts must run in chronological or fiscal chronological order.
issues.action: Sort MonthName by a numeric MonthNumber or FiscalMonthIndex column. Prefer a proper date field on a continuous axis when showing a single period, and preserve the FiscalYear legend only if year-over-year seasonal comparison is intended.

issues.observed: TotalRevenue and YoYGrowthPct share a revenue-scaled axis. Revenue columns dominate while the growth series collapses into an almost invisible red line near zero.
issues.desired: Revenue and growth should both be readable without implying that currency and percentage values share a common scale.
issues.action: Use a line and clustered column chart with revenue as columns, YoY growth as a line, and a clearly labeled secondary percentage axis. Apply conditional red or green to growth based on sign rather than assigning red to all growth values.

issues.observed: Category revenue bars are visible, but YoYGrowthPct is compressed against the origin and cannot be compared across categories.
issues.desired: The category view should support simultaneous comparison of category size and growth risk.
issues.action: Keep horizontal revenue bars for ranking and place YoY growth in a separate aligned percentage panel, data-label column, or accessible native visual beside the bars. Use green for positive growth and red for negative growth without converting or rescaling the underlying measure.

issues.observed: No visible date, region, or category filters are available, and the current filter context is not communicated.
issues.desired: Executives should have compact, consistently positioned Date Range, Region, and Category controls with an obvious reset action.
issues.action: Add a top filter strip containing date range, region, and category slicers plus a reset-filters bookmark button. Keep slicers compact and show the active reporting period even when the filter pane is collapsed.

issues.observed: Titles expose model field names such as TotalRevenue, GrossMarginPct, MonthName, FiscalYear, RegionName, and CategoryName.
issues.desired: Titles and legends should use concise business language appropriate for a CEO/CFO audience.
issues.action: Replace autogenerated titles with Revenue Trend, Gross Margin % Trend, Regional Performance, and Category Performance. Rename displayed series to Revenue and YoY Growth, and use subtitles only where fiscal-year comparison needs explanation.

issues.observed: The canvas has no visible Executive Overview heading, reporting-period subtitle, or clear separation between KPI summary and supporting analysis.
issues.desired: The page should immediately identify its purpose and current reporting scope.
issues.action: Add a compact Executive Overview header with a dynamic reporting-period subtitle. Group the four KPIs into consistent card containers and align the trend and performance sections to a clear grid.

issues.observed: KPI cards show only current values. They provide no prior-period comparison, directional indicator, target status, or explanation of why 14 risk areas matter.
issues.desired: The executive summary should distinguish performance, momentum, and risk at a glance.
issues.action: Add compact prior-year or target variance beneath each value where supported by approved measures. For Risk Areas, use a warning treatment and provide drill-through or a tooltip listing the principal risk dimensions; do not infer status from the count without a defined threshold.

issues.observed: Green is used for revenue and red for the entire growth series, regardless of whether growth is positive or negative. Red therefore functions both as a series color and an implied warning.
issues.desired: Neutral or brand colors should identify measures, while green and red should be reserved for favorable and unfavorable status.
issues.action: Adopt a restrained executive palette such as blue for revenue and a neutral dark tone for margin. Apply green and red conditionally to growth and risk states, with accessible contrast and non-color labels.

issues.observed: Month labels are small, angled, and truncated in places. Axis titles repeat technical field names and consume space without improving comprehension.
issues.desired: Time labels should be easy to scan, and axis text should use concise units.
issues.action: After correcting chronological sorting, use abbreviated horizontal month labels where space permits, reduce unnecessary axis titles, and format axes as £K/£M and percentages. Increase key label size slightly for boardroom viewing.

issues.observed: The value 14 is visually indistinguishable from the other unlabeled KPIs, so the page does not communicate whether it is acceptable, worsening, or urgent.
issues.desired: Risk should be visually distinct but governed by an approved threshold or comparison measure.
issues.action: Label the card Risk Areas and add an approved change-versus-prior-period or severity indicator. Use red only when the business rule classifies the count as adverse; otherwise use neutral styling.

issues.observed: A prominent trial-capacity banner appears above the report and materially reduces executive credibility.
issues.desired: The production dashboard should open without licensing or trial notices.
issues.action: Deploy the report to appropriately licensed production capacity or resolve the tenant/capacity configuration. This cannot be corrected through report theme or canvas formatting.

issues.observed: Large blank areas surround the KPI numbers, while chart plotting areas remain relatively shallow. The page feels like an unfinished default report rather than a deliberate executive layout.
issues.desired: Whitespace should organize content while preserving enough plotting area for meaningful comparisons.
issues.action: Reduce the height of the KPI band, use consistent card padding and borders, and reallocate vertical space to the trend and performance charts. Maintain the existing clean two-column alignment.

summary: The deployed page contains the required KPI and chart types and has a reasonably aligned two-column foundation, but it is not yet board-ready. Missing KPI labels and filters, non-chronological month sorting, unreadable mixed-scale growth series, technical field-name titles, weak risk context, and the trial banner significantly undermine analytical trust and executive polish. Most deficiencies are achievable Power BI design, modeling, theme, and layout fixes; the trial notice requires deployment or licensing remediation.
reference_rejected_ideas: Pixel-perfect replication of the Power BI application header and left navigation rail is non-analytical and should not be recreated inside the report canvas.

The reference's horizontal revenue bars with overlaid growth dots and a separate percentage axis are not straightforward in native Power BI. A custom visual may introduce governance and accessibility concerns; aligned native visuals or a labeled growth column are safer.
Decorative KPI sparklines should only be added when a valid time-grain measure and sufficient space are available. They should not replace explicit period comparisons or status logic.
Information icons on every card are unnecessary unless they open useful metric definitions or governed tooltip content.
